title: People’s Mañanera September 23
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**2,400 km of New Passenger Rail Lines  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum announced that an additional 2,400 km of
passenger rail lines have been laid, representing an investment of 750 billion
pesos (US$42.90 billion) and creating 88,000 direct jobs. “The Transformation
brought about the revival of passenger rail service”, with greater regional
connectivity, more jobs, and shorter travel times, she said.

**Social Programs Reach Millions of Households  
** In Mexico, more than 4 out of every 10 households receive at least one
government social program, 41.4% of the total. In addition, access to social
security and healthcare increased from 77.1% of families in 2020 to 86.6% in
2025.

**Mexico: No to Foreign Interference in Brazil  
** Sheinbaum emphasized that Brazilian President Lula fulfilled his “Zero
Hunger” commitment and reiterated her support for the principle of self-
determination. “There should be no foreign interference in any election in any
country. In Brazil, let the Brazilians decide freely,” she declared.

**To Represent Mexico, a Single Citizenship  
** Regarding the approved constitutional reform, Sheinbaum maintained that it
does not take away the rights of Mexicans living abroad. “To be president, you
cannot swear allegiance to two flags. You represent Mexico and no one else,”
she stated.

**Lie Detector**

  * It is not true that the 2027 Fiscal Package seeks to impose a 3% tax on sales of companies with tax losses and that it will drive public debt to record levels
  * It is not true that the Mexican government seeks to censor parodies, memes, and criticism of the government through modifications to the Federal Copyright Law.
  * It is not true that more than 3 million pesos (US$172,000) from the public treasury were allocated to purchase clothing for President Claudia Sheinbaum.
  * It is not true that Sheinbaum’s presidential report back event in Querétaro was “empty.”
  * It is not true that Mexico is losing its appeal as a tourist destination and that the number of international visitors to the country is declining
